rationale: At n=100,000 I predict the heap wins for K up to about 5,000. The heap pays O(n) root comparisons plus O(K log K) consolidation; the bounded buffer pays O(K) shifting whenever a record enters, and about K ln(n/K) records enter. I expect full sort (n log n) to overtake the heap around K=10,000. Buffer should only be competitive for very small K, probably below K=100.
Heap maintains only K records and pays n root comparisons. Bounded buffer shifts O(K) on accepted records. Full sort ignores K and becomes competitive only when K is a large fraction of n.
